clue.text: Caring girl taking a crook in hand

definitions.text: Caring girl taking a crook in hand

parts.words: Caring girl taking a crook in hand
parts.note: a young woman who tends a flock and carries the hooked staff of her trade, not a girl befriending a criminal

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted young woman takes a villain under her wing to reform him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal and 'taking in hand' like reforming him; the crook is the hooked staff a flock-minder carries.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the female keeper of sheep, whose traditional tool is a hooked staff.

clue.text: Exhibit some leaning for a blackguard

explanation.surface: Someone showing slightly slanted opinions is a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heels tilts over to one side; and a heel is a contemptible, dishonourable man, a cad.

clue.text: To Americans this is plain

parts.note: plain is the noun for flat open grassland, here the vast flat grasslands of the North American interior, not the adjective meaning obvious

explanation.surface: Something seems perfectly obvious to people in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' reads as 'obvious', but it is the noun: a broad treeless grassland of the American Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: The great flat grasslands of the central United States are called by this name.

clue.text: Sound exercise for certain animals

indicators.note: the word Sound at the start says the next word's synonym is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to exercise a right or tool is to use it

explanation.surface: Healthy activity is recommended for some creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound exercise' looks like healthy activity; 'Sound' is the homophone signal on USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep are a particular kind of farm animal.

clue.text: Drier it may be, but more polluted

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters of the words before could be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: Something may be less damp, yet it is also dirtier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' signals the anagram of DRIER IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more polluted is filthier, carrying more grime.

clue.text: Set up a north and a south Yemen capital

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the pieces are written from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Instructions to establish northern and southern capitals in Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reverses A, N, A, S, which read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sana (Sanaa) is the chief city and seat of government of Yemen.

clue.text: The player's increasing speed

parts.note: a musician is told by a score marking to play gradually faster, rather than an athlete speeding up

explanation.surface: A sportsman is getting quicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a sportsman; it is a musician, and the answer is the Italian tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction instructs the performer to gradually quicken the tempo.

clue.text: Fellows around the city misheard the figures

indicators.note: around tells us the fellows' word goes outside the remaining pieces

parts.note: dons are fellows of a university college
EC is the postcode area for the City of London
read as mis-heard: the letters of heard, mis-arranged

explanation.surface: College fellows in the City got the numbers wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misheard' looks like a homophone signal, but read it as 'heard' mixed up. EC is the City of London's postcode; 'around' puts the fellows outside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: These solid shapes are polyhedra with ten faces, geometrical figures.

clue.text: A bigamist's euro-babble?

parts.note: a man with two wives, a 'Dutch' being old slang for a wife, and also incomprehensible talk in a European tongue

explanation.surface: The confused talk of a man married to two women at once.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney slang 'Dutch' (from 'Duchess of Fife') is a wife, so a bigamist has two; the phrase also means gibberish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unintelligible speech or jargon, literally a doubled wife in slang.

clue.text: An infant prodigy — hardly surprising!

explanation.surface: A gifted young child, yet no one is astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a tiny marvel, a gifted child; as an idiom, 'no wonder', meaning it is to be expected.

clue.text: Going up

parts.note: read as getting onto a mount and riding, not ascending in a lift

explanation.surface: Something is rising or ascending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' suggests ascending; read it as mounting and travelling in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Equestrian activity begins by mounting the animal, being 'up' on its back.

clue.text: Co2 left to freeze

parts.note: read as C followed by O twice, the 2 doubling the O

explanation.surface: Carbon dioxide left out will freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Co2' looks like carbon dioxide but is C plus two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill something down is to lower its temperature, as in letting feelings or food freeze.

clue.text: Duck behind a doctor's reading-desk

indicators.note: behind says the duck's letter comes after the other pieces, at the back

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
a duck is a nil score in cricket, the round figure O

explanation.surface: A duck sits behind the physician's lectern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a zero score in cricket, the round letter, and 'behind' puts it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised stand or pulpit in early churches from which scripture is read.

clue.text: Rile mob agitator to distract

indicators.note: an agitator stirs things up, so the letters of the words before are stirred

explanation.surface: A troublemaker winds up the crowd to divert attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitator' signals the anagram of RILE MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to throw into confusion or entangle, distracting and disturbing.

clue.text: A course for the egg-producer

explanation.surface: A course for a laying hen.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is one course or tier of material, as of bricks; and a hen that lays eggs.

clue.text: Pollutes gorges

explanation.surface: Something pollutes narrow ravines.
explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to make dirty or corrupt; defiles are narrow mountain passes or ravines.

clue.text: The people engaged in trade mostly

annotationWithheld.why: 'The people engaged in trade mostly': DEMOS fits 'The people', but no reading of 'engaged in trade mostly' gives the letters, and no source found gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: The people engaged in trade mostly

clue.text: Forever acquiring silver — really keen

indicators.note: acquiring means the word for forever takes in the next piece

parts.note: e'er is the poetic shortening of ever, meaning always
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone always gaining silver is truly enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The poetic contraction e'er for 'ever' supplies the outer letters, with the chemical symbol for silver held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager is being very keen and impatient to do something.

clue.text: Scanned a newspaper leader about the old

indicators.note: about tells us the editor's abbreviation goes around the other piece

parts.note: the editor leads a newspaper, abbreviated ED
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A paper's editor scanned something about old times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper leader' looks like an editorial; it is the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have eyed something is to have looked at or examined it, as one scans text.

clue.text: Riotous characters were put in jug

indicators.note: the characters, i.e. letters, of the next word run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Unruly people were thrown into prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' is slang for prison in the surface but here a pitcher; 'Riotous characters' signals the anagram of WERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed pitcher for water.

clue.text: Note one retired to a place in Italy

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word one is written backwards

explanation.surface: A musical note retired to live in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the word one backwards; a 'place' here is a city, not a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a port city in northwest Italy.

clue.text: Back up say over nicer alternative in general

indicators.note: in a down clue back up means the abbreviation is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means

indicators.note: alternative signals a different arrangement of the letters of nicer

explanation.surface: Support a nicer option in general terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back up' reverses EG to GE; 'alternative' turns NICER into NERIC; 'over' places GE above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something generic applies to a whole class rather than a specific case.

clue.text: Person charging a consumer about two hundred

indicators.note: about means the first pieces are placed around the number

parts.note: a user consumes something
CC is two hundred in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone accuses a consumer of spending around two hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the Roman numeral for two hundred inside a + consumer; 'charging' is accusing, not billing.
explanation.definitionFit: An accuser is one who brings a charge or allegation against someone.

clue.text: Neighbour preparing a spread

parts.note: butter is spread on bread

explanation.surface: A neighbour is making something to put on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparing' links A + BUTTER (a spread) to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutter is one whose property borders another's, a person living next door.

clue.text: Made a point about short name being disdained

indicators.note: about means scored goes around the letter for name

parts.note: to score is to make a point in a game
N is the short form of name

explanation.surface: Someone argued about an abbreviated name and was looked down on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a point' sounds like arguing, but it is scoring in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To be scorned is to be treated with contempt, held in disdain.

clue.text: Pipe cut off by small daughter

parts.note: D is the short form of daughter

indicators.note: off means the letters of cut are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A pipe gets cut by a little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals an anagram of CUT, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a tube or channel carrying fluid or air.

clue.text: Thanks repeatedly when saying goodbye

indicators.note: repeatedly means the short word for thanks is given twice

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Saying thank you over and over when taking leave.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal for thanks; doubled it is a childish farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is informal British for farewell, see you later.

clue.text: Her make-up is in rainbow colours!

definitions.text: Her make-up is in rainbow colours!

parts.words: Her make-up is in rainbow colours!
parts.note: the Greek goddess personifying the rainbow, also a flower and the coloured ring of the eye, not a woman wearing gaudy cosmetics

explanation.surface: A woman wears garish multicoloured cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics; she is the Greek goddess of the rainbow, and her name also means the coloured part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the messenger goddess was the personified rainbow.

clue.text: Stitched according to directions

parts.note: S, E, W and N are the compass directions south, east, west and north
S, E, W and N are the compass directions south, east, west and north
S, E, W and N are the compass directions south, east, west and north
S, E, W and N are the compass directions south, east, west and north

explanation.surface: Something was stitched following the instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'directions' looks like instructions; it is four compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sewn has been joined with needle and thread.

clue.text: Oriental coppers hold one key and that's marked

indicators.note: hold means the coins' name contains the next piece

parts.note: the sen is a small copper coin of Japan and other Far Eastern countries
E is one musical key

explanation.surface: Eastern policemen are holding a key, and that has been noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police; they are coins, the sen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seen has been noticed or observed, as a thing marked is.

clue.text: Cropping expert

parts.note: someone skilled at cutting short, of hair on heads rather than harvesting crops

explanation.surface: A specialist in harvesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cropping' suggests farming; it is cutting hair short.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional cuts and styles people's locks.

clue.text: Take stock of the season to ensure good timing

parts.note: to watch is to observe and take stock of
spring is a season of the year

explanation.surface: Assess the season so the schedule runs smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take stock of' sounds like accounting but means observe.
explanation.definitionFit: The coiled spring in a timepiece drives its movement, keeping it accurate.
